title: Canonical open-slice restriction comparison and its shriek adjunct
statement: Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, put $R_T=p_T^*R$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $\mathcal M_R(T)=\operatorname{Mod}_{R_T}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories and the actual geometric derived adjunctions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $b:W\to V$, $a:W\to U$, $j:V\to X$, and $c:U\to X$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], and use the exact extension by zero $b_!,c_!$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. For a commuting square $jb=ca$ and $K\in D(\mathcal M_R(W))$, define the canonical restriction comparison $t_{R,K}:c^*Rj_*b_!K\to Ra_*K$ as the canonical derived exchange mate $c^*Rj_*\to Ra_*b^*$ [def-sfb-derived-exchange-scalar-comparisons], evaluated at $b_!K$, followed by $Ra_*$ of the inverse of the actual open unit $u_{b,R,K}:K\to b^*b_!K$. The exact-pullback identifications between total derived and levelwise pullback are the canonical ones. The unit $u_b$ is invertible. When the square is cartesian, $t_{R,K}$ is invertible. For such a cartesian square define $e_{R,K}:c_!Ra_*K\to Rj_*b_!K$ to be the $c_!\dashv c^*$ adjunct of $t_{R,K}^{-1}$. The helper declarations give $\mathcal M_R(T)$, $u_b$ invertibility, $t_R$, its invertibility in a cartesian open square, and $e_R$. No quasi-compactness, tameness, field hypothesis, or invertibility of $e_R$ is imposed.
